counterfactual_missing_items: absence of documented immune deficiency or STI history
no explicit mention of SCC risk factors beyond atypical cells
decisive_items: Gram stain and cultures were negative
no fistula to the anal canal
response.rationale: R3 is supported by the presence of atypical squamous cells and the explicit inclusion of squamous cell carcinoma in the differential, while the negative cultures and lack of a true anal fistula undermine R4 and R1. R4 is a plausible runner-up due to purulent fluid and recurrent abscesses, but the negative microbiology and cytologic atypia favor malignancy.

rejected.why: Purulent fluid and recurrent abscesses are present, but negative cultures and atypical squamous cells argue against a simple abscess; the mass enlarged despite drainage.
An external sinus tract is noted, but the explicit absence of a fistula to the anal canal contradicts the diagnosis of anorectal fistula.
